ABOUT MATTER LABS

Matter Labs builds infrastructure for financial sovereignty. We pioneered zero-knowledge rollups on Ethereum and developed the Prividium platform to help financial institutions build and operate digital asset businesses with privacy and control.
The platform’s adoption spans global finance, from DTCC, a cornerstone of securities markets, to Cari’s network of 30 banks representing $10 trillion in combined assets.

We’re a remote, global team tackling hard problems in cryptography and finance. Expect autonomy, high standards and access to the best AI tools. Your work will help shape how financial institutions move and manage money.




THE ROLE

You join the Platform team, which designs and builds the ZKsync OS node. You own one or more of its core systems end to end: peer-to-peer networking, consensus, RPC, the sequencer or storage, depending on where your depth is. We are looking first for depth in consensus or peer-to-peer networking, and next in high-performance storage. You also bring new protocol features into the node, such as cross-chain interoperability and new zero-knowledge provers.

The Production Unit runs the node for customers, and the Platform team makes sure what it runs is correct. The role has no customer-facing work. When an incident touches a system you own, the Production Unit can pull you in during your working hours.

What you will do:

 - Own core node systems. Design, build and maintain one or more of networking, consensus, RPC, sequencing or storage, and decide how they evolve.

 - Integrate new protocol features. Bring features such as interoperability and new provers into the node without breaking existing behaviour or the upgrade path.

 - Design bugs out. Use the type system, architecture, property-based testing and fuzzing so whole classes of bugs never reach production.

 - Hold the review bar. Review your colleagues' code as carefully as you write your own, and expect the same from them.

 - Use AI with judgment. Use the best AI tools to move faster, and understand every line you merge, whoever or whatever wrote it.

Within a year, you own one or two of the node's core systems, and features land in them without regressions.




WHAT WE LOOK FOR

 - You have designed and built a core component of a distributed system, blockchain node or database: networking, consensus, storage, an RPC layer or similar.

 - You write strong systems code in Rust, C++, Go or a comparable language. Our node is written in Rust, and Rust is learnable here.

 - You use types and architecture to make invalid states unrepresentable, and you have used property-based testing or fuzzing on real code.

 - Your code reviews find real problems, and you can explain every line you ship.

 - You can take a protocol change from specification to a running system without breaking what already works.

Nice to have: Ethereum execution or consensus client internals; RocksDB or another high-performance storage engine; zero-knowledge provers; libp2p or a comparable networking stack; open-source systems work we can read.

If you meet most of this and the rest is learnable, apply anyway.





COMPENSATION AND WORK MODEL

 - Base salary range: USD 150,000 to 187,000 per year. Where an offer lands in the range depends on demonstrated scope and results against the bar described above. The same range applies wherever you are based.

 - Performance-based variable compensation and a long-term token incentive are additional.

 - Benefits (employees): medical, dental and vision from day one, global health cover for team members outside the US; 401(k) with a Safe Harbor match up to 4 percent for eligible US employees, flexible paid time off plus public holidays and two company closure weeks a year; six weeks paid parental bonding leave plus up to ten weeks paid birth recovery leave; confidential mental health support; a USD 2,000 home office stipend, a company laptop refreshed every three years, up to USD 400 a month toward coworking, and a USD 500 annual learning budget; company and team offsites.

 - Fully remote, from any country where we can hire. Your working hours overlap with European or US time zones. Time zones close to Europe fit the team best.

 - Full-time, as an employee or a contractor.
